title: PostgreSQL indexes
text: A B-tree index speeds up equality and range lookups on a column. Create it with CREATE INDEX on the columns used in WHERE and ORDER BY clauses. Every index slows down writes, because inserts and updates must also maintain the index. Use EXPLAIN ANALYZE to confirm that the planner actually uses an index instead of a sequential scan.

title: PostgreSQL vacuum
text: PostgreSQL uses MVCC, so updated and deleted rows leave dead tuples behind. The autovacuum daemon removes dead tuples and updates planner statistics. If autovacuum falls behind, tables bloat and queries slow down. VACUUM FULL rewrites the table and takes an exclusive lock, so prefer regular VACUUM.

title: Connection pooling
text: Opening a database connection is expensive, so applications reuse connections from a pool. PgBouncer sits between the application and PostgreSQL and multiplexes many clients over few server connections. In transaction pooling mode a connection returns to the pool after each transaction, which breaks session-level features such as prepared statements.

title: Schema migrations
text: Alembic tracks schema changes as versioned migration scripts. Each revision has an upgrade and a downgrade function. Autogenerate compares the SQLAlchemy models with the live database and drafts a migration, but the draft must be reviewed because it can miss renamed columns. Never edit a migration that has already been applied in production.

title: FastAPI dependency injection
text: FastAPI resolves function parameters declared with Depends before calling the endpoint. Dependencies can open a database session, check an authentication token or validate query parameters. A dependency that uses yield runs cleanup code after the response is sent. Dependencies can be overridden in tests with app.dependency_overrides.

title: FastAPI async endpoints
text: Endpoints declared with async def run on the event loop and must not block. Calling a blocking library such as requests or a synchronous database driver inside async code freezes every other request. Plain def endpoints run in a thread pool instead. Use asyncio-friendly clients like httpx and asyncpg for IO inside async endpoints.

title: Request validation
text: FastAPI uses Pydantic models to validate request bodies and generate OpenAPI documentation. Invalid input produces an automatic 422 response that lists each failing field. Field constraints such as min_length or ge are declared on the model. Response models filter the output so that internal fields like password hashes are never returned.

title: Celery retries
text: Celery tasks can retry on failure with a countdown or exponential backoff. Set autoretry_for to the exception classes that are worth retrying and retry_backoff to space the attempts. Tasks must be idempotent because a retry or a worker crash can run the same task twice. Set a maximum number of retries so a poisoned message does not loop forever.

title: Celery brokers
text: A Celery broker carries task messages between producers and workers. Redis is simple to run but can lose messages if the server restarts without persistence. RabbitMQ offers durable queues and acknowledgements. With acks_late the message is acknowledged only after the task finishes, so a crashed worker does not lose the task.

title: Redis caching
text: Redis can cache expensive query results with a time to live. The cache-aside pattern checks Redis first and falls back to the database on a miss, then stores the result. Choose a TTL that matches how stale data may be. Stampedes happen when many requests miss the same expired key at once, so use locking or jittered expiry.

title: Docker image layers
text: Each instruction in a Dockerfile creates a layer, and unchanged layers are cached. Copy the dependency manifest and install packages before copying the application source, so code edits do not invalidate the install layer. Multi-stage builds compile in one image and copy only the artifacts into a small runtime image. A .dockerignore file keeps the build context small.

title: Docker Compose
text: Docker Compose describes several containers in one YAML file. Services reach each other by service name on a shared network. A healthcheck lets dependent services wait until the database accepts connections. Named volumes keep database files after the container is removed.

title: GitLab CI/CD
text: A GitLab pipeline is defined in .gitlab-ci.yml and runs in stages such as test, build and deploy. Jobs in the same stage run in parallel on runners. Cache keys speed up dependency installation between pipeline runs. Protected variables hold deployment secrets and are exposed only to protected branches.

title: Git branching
text: Gitflow uses long-lived main and develop branches plus short-lived feature branches. Feature branches merge into develop through pull requests that are reviewed. Release branches stabilise a version before it is merged into main and tagged. Rebasing a feature branch onto develop keeps history linear but rewrites commits, so never rebase a shared branch.

title: Chunking for RAG
text: Documents are split into chunks before they are embedded. Chunks that are too large dilute the embedding and waste prompt tokens, while chunks that are too small lose context. Splitting on sentence boundaries with a small overlap keeps meaning intact across chunk edges. Store the document title with each chunk so answers can cite their source.

title: Hybrid search
text: Keyword search with BM25 finds exact terms such as error codes and product names. Vector search finds passages with similar meaning even when the words differ. Hybrid retrieval runs both and merges the rankings, commonly with reciprocal rank fusion. Fusion needs no score normalisation because it uses only the rank positions.

title: Evaluating retrieval
text: Retrieval quality is measured against a labelled set of questions with known relevant documents. Recall at k is the share of questions whose relevant document appears in the top k results. Mean reciprocal rank rewards placing the relevant document near the top. Evaluate retrieval separately from generation so that a bad answer can be traced to its cause.

title: Reducing hallucinations
text: A language model can state false facts confidently. Grounding the answer in retrieved passages and requiring citations reduces this. The prompt should tell the model to say that it does not know when the context lacks the answer. Setting the temperature to zero makes answers more repeatable but does not by itself make them correct.

title: GDPR right to erasure
text: Under the GDPR a person can ask a controller to delete their personal data. Systems need a way to find and remove that data from databases, backups with defined retention, and derived stores such as search indexes and vector databases. Keep an audit log of the deletion request itself without storing the deleted content. Respond to requests within one month.

title: JWT authentication
text: A JSON Web Token carries signed claims such as the user id and an expiry time. The server verifies the signature without a database lookup. Keep access tokens short-lived and use a refresh token to obtain new ones. A token cannot be revoked before it expires unless the server keeps a denylist, so avoid putting sensitive data in the payload because it is only encoded, not encrypted.
